title: Dired undo does not restore filesystem changes

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: `dired-undo' undoes changes in the Dired buffer; it explicitly does not recover files removed from the filesystem.
hypothesis: After a real file is deleted, attempting `dired-undo' should not recreate the deleted file; any undo effect is limited to Dired-buffer state.
minimal_fixture: One temporary directory, one file, one Dired buffer mark, and one real filesystem deletion.
predicted_behavior: The recovery attempt is a Dired-buffer operation; the deleted file remains absent.
observed_behavior: mark-before=42 undo-result=(error "(user-error \"No further undo information\")") mark-after=nil file-exists-after-dired-undo=nil

independent_checks.name: dired mark existed before filesystem deletion

counterexample: A generic recovery strategy that runs undo after a Dired action can fail to undo even buffer-local state and still leaves destructive filesystem state unrecovered.
derived_gym_requirement: Dired benchmarks must grade filesystem state independently from Dired buffer state and must classify destructive file operations as externally consequential.
